messages:
leo: Opening a docs PR for packaging & signing PKCS#11 HSM kernel modules and DKMS flow for air-gapped Private installs. Goal: show RHEL/SLES/Deb workflows, module signing (MOK), and offline repo layout. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/ZZAA. Need eng-sre + security review.

anya: 👍 This is great. Two immediate asks: (1) please include the exact mokutil workflow for enrolling the module signing key, (2) show how to generate the private key in an HSM or use an ephemeral signing VM for air-gapped sites.

paul: For DKMS: include steps to build + package driver with DKMS.conf and example rpm/deb packaging snippets. Also call out differences for older kernels where dkms fails and we must ship prebuilt .ko.

sre-ops: Add a note about Secure Boot: if customers have secure boot enabled, they must enroll the MOK before booting the host with the new module. Provide an example one-liner to check Secure Boot status: `mokutil --sb-state`.

leo: Draft snippets I'll include below. Please poke holes.

```
# example offline bundle layout (tarball root)
opt/offline-bundle/
  README.md
  sign-key/
    module-signing.pem
    module-signing.key
    signature-checksums.txt
  packages/
    rhel/ (rpms)
    debian/ (debs)
  modules/
    hsm-driver-1.2.3.ko
  scripts/
    postinstall.sh
```

leo: Module sign example (on-airgap-signing-host):

```bash
# generate key and cert (recommended: generate key on an HSM or dedicated signing host)
openssl req -new -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -days 3650 -nodes -subj "/CN=redwood-module-signing" -keyout module-signing.key -out module-signing.pem
# sign module
/sbin/sign-file sha256 module-signing.key module-signing.pem hsm-driver-1.2.3.ko
# verify
modinfo -F signer hsm-driver-1.2.3.ko
```

paul: For DKMS packaging add DKMS.conf snippet and example spec file to build an rpm that installs /usr/src/hsm-driver-1.2.3 and registers it with dkms. If kernel headers are missing on target, fall back to shipping prebuilt .ko and an install script that places it into /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/... and runs `depmod -a`.

anya: For MOK enrollment include the bootstrap commands for interactive and unattended flows. Example interactive: `mokutil --import module-signing.pem` then reboot and follow MOK manager. For unattended (air-gapped) use shim-signed or pre-enroll via efivars in the offline bundle if customer consents. Document security tradeoffs.

leo: Adding systemd postinstall snippet to place module and run depmod + trigger DKMS: 

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
# if using prebuilt
cp modules/hsm-driver-1.2.3.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/
/sbin/depmod -a
modprobe hsm_driver || true
# log outcome
logger -t redwood-installer "hsm-driver install: $(modinfo -F signer /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/hsm-driver-1.2.3.ko 2>/dev/null || echo unsigned)"
```

sre-ops: Add SELinux note: if targeted policy is enforced, include `semanage fcontext`/`restorecon` steps for module path or advise temporarily setting permissive for install.

paul: Also include a small RPM signing & repo creation snippet: `rpm --addsign *.rpm` on signing host, `createrepo_c .` for offline yum repo. For Debian: `dpkg-sig --sign builder *.deb` and `dpkg-scanpackages . /dev/null | gzip -9c > Packages.gz`.

anya: Troubleshooting table please: symptom / check / fix. Examples: 
- "modprobe: ERROR: could not insert" -> check `dmesg | grep -i 'signature'` and `mokutil --sb-state` -> enroll key or disable secure boot.
- "pkcs11-tool can't open token" -> check driver loaded (`lsmod | grep hsm_driver`) and `modinfo` signer.

leo: I'll also add a short 'how to sign with an HSM' blurb: generate CSR on signing host, use vendor PKCS#11 tool to sign and export PEM, then use sign-file with HSM-signed cert and private key via PKCS11 engine examples.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/ZZAA (files: docs/private/module-signing-hsm.md, examples/offline-bundle-module.md, snippets/dkms-specs.md)

paul: One more security nit: recommend rotating signing key annually and include an example revoke workflow (replace module, re-enroll new MOK, schedule reboots).

leo: Great. I'll push the PR updates and add a checklist item "eng-sre smoke on a Secure Boot enabled VM". Thanks all, will ping when it's ready for final review.
